ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle B=90^\circ$, $\angle BCA=60^\circ$, $AC=2\sqrt{2}$, $DA=1$, $CD=3$. Find the area of quadrilateral $ABCD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given $\because$ $\angle B=90^\circ$, $\angle BCA=60^\circ$, $\therefore$ $\angle A=30^\circ$, $\therefore$ BC=$\frac{1}{2}$AC=$\sqrt{2}$, AB=$\sqrt{6}$, $\because$ AC=2$\sqrt{2}$, DA=1, CD=3, $\therefore$ AC$^{2}$+DA$^{2}$=9=CD$^{2}$, $\therefore$ $\angle CAD=90^\circ$, $\therefore$ $S_{\text{quadrilateral} ABCD}=S_{\triangle ABC}+S_{\triangle ACD}$, =$\frac{1}{2}\cdot$AB$\cdot$BC+$\frac{1}{2}\cdot$AC$\cdot$DA, =$\frac{1}{2}\times\sqrt{6}\times\sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{2}\times2\sqrt{2}\times1$, =$\boxed{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle B=90^\circ$, $\angle BCA=60^\circ$, $AC=2\sqrt{2}$, $DA=1$, $CD=3$. Find the area of quadrilateral $ABCD$.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given $\because$ $\angle B=90^\circ$, $\angle BCA=60^\circ$, $\therefore$ $\angle A=30^\circ$, $\therefore$ BC=$\frac{1}{2}$AC=$\sqrt{2}$, AB=$\sqrt{6}$, $\because$ AC=2$\sqrt{2}$, DA=1, CD=3, $\therefore$ AC$^{2}$+DA$^{2}$=9=CD$^{2}$, $\therefore$ $\angle CAD=90^\circ$, $\therefore$ $S_{\text{quadrilateral} ABCD}=S_{\triangle ABC}+S_{\triangle ACD}$, =$\frac{1}{2}\cdot$AB$\cdot$BC+$\frac{1}{2}\cdot$AC$\cdot$DA, =$\frac{1}{2}\times\sqrt{6}\times\sqrt{2}+\frac{1}{2}\times2\sqrt{2}\times1$, =$\boxed{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure is quadrilateral ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left; segment AC is drawn and is located inside the quadrilateral, dividing the quadrilateral into triangle ABC and triangle ACD. There is a right-angle mark at point B, indicating that AB is perpendicular to BC. D and B are respectively located on the two sides of diagonal AC, so the area of quadrilateral ABCD can be obtained by adding the areas of triangle ABC and triangle ACD.

Then reason: In triangle ABC, it is known that angle B = 90°, angle BCA = 60°, so angle BAC = 30°. AC = 2sqrt(2) is the hypotenuse of right triangle ABC. By the property of a 30°-60°-90° triangle, BC is the side opposite 30°, so BC = AC/2 = sqrt(2); AB = sqrt(3)·BC = sqrt(6). Therefore the area of triangle ABC is (1/2)·AB·BC = (1/2)·sqrt(6)·sqrt(2) = sqrt(3).

In triangle ACD, AC = 2sqrt(2), AD = 1, CD = 3. Calculate AC^2 + AD^2 = (2sqrt(2))^2 + 1^2 = 8 + 1 = 9 = CD^2, so according to the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, angle CAD = 90°. Therefore the area of triangle ACD is (1/2)·AC·AD = (1/2)·2sqrt(2)·1 = sqrt(2).

So the area of quadrilateral ABCD is sqrt(3) + sqrt(2).
